title: agent-guardrails workspace manifest
description: The root manifest of a monorepo. It names the packages — each of which carries its own guardrails.config.json — and holds the repo-level checks that have no source tree of their own. It is deliberately NOT guardrails.config.json: the oxlint plugin resolves that filename from process.cwd(), so a root file under that name would let a root-level oxlint run lint every package against one config and silently disable the checks each package declares ownedByLinter. Under this name, a root-level oxlint run fails closed at plugin load instead.

$schema.description: Path to this schema, for editor completion.

version.description: Manifest version. run.sh warns when it trails the scripts' version.

items.description: Repo-relative directory, no leading or trailing slash and no ".." segment — e.g. "packages/database". run.sh cd's into each of these, so a traversal here would take the whole gate outside the repo.

packages.description: Every package guardrails governs. Each must exist on disk and hold a guardrails.config.json; either failure exits 3 rather than being skipped. minItems is 1 because an empty list is indistinguishable from a manifest nobody finished writing, and it would make the whole gate pass while checking nothing.

bannedDeps.description: Dependencies rejected in the ROOT package.json. Each package's own config still governs its own manifest.

neverTracked.description: Paths git must never track. In a workspace these are repo-relative and every package's secret file needs listing — wrangler reads .dev.vars beside each wrangler.jsonc, so naming only the root one silently leaves the others unguarded.

why.description: What breaks when the shadow wins. Required — a rule whose reason is unwritten gets deleted by the next person who trips over it.

shadowConfigs.description: Config files at the ROOT that shadow the real one.

requiredFiles.description: Files the workspace ROOT must have.
